material_definitions: Samples in the LiHf2(PO4)3 + 0.3Li2O system were prepared by sintering at various temperatures: 1073 K, 1173 K, 1293 K, and 1393 K.
The ionic conductivity was measured using AC impedance and is presented as a function of temperature in an Arrhenius-style plot.
The plot displays log(sigma*T) vs 1000/T, where sigma is the ionic conductivity.
Conductivity values vary significantly depending on the sintering temperature, with the 1293 K sample showing the highest performance.

The LiHf2(PO4)3 + yLi2O system is a NASICON-type solid electrolyte material.
It explores the effect of excess Li2O addition (y = 0 to 0.4) on densification and conductivity.
The ceramic samples were prepared by sintering at temperatures ranging from 1050 K to 1600 K.
Total ionic conductivity was determined at room temperature (298 K) using impedance spectroscopy.
The addition of Li2O significantly improves conductivity by four orders of magnitude compared to pure LiHf2(PO4)3.

Solid solutions of the type Li1+xMxHf2-x(PO4)3 where M is a trivalent cation (Cr, Fe, Sc, In, Lu, or Y) substituted for Hf4+.
The substitution is accompanied by the addition of Li+ for charge compensation.
The graph shows the total ionic conductivity as a function of the substitution level x.
Measurements were performed at a constant temperature of 298 K.
